visual: Deeply cut leaves under dense white felt · almost white in the border
water: Moderate at first · let it dry between waterings
prune: Trim untidy growth · take the flower stems off to keep it silver
toxicity: Potentially harmful if eaten; sap may irritate sensitive skin.
hardinessNote: Hardy in coastal and relatively mild UK locations, approximately -5 to 1°C; often treated as seasonal bedding in colder areas.
resilience: Drought and coastal tolerant but dislikes cold wet winters
uses: Bedding · edging · pots · coastal planting · silver schemes
uncertain: Nursery label 'Cineraria Silver Leaf' appears to be a generic trade description rather than a securely identifiable cultivar. (Oscar's note.)

peak: research said "Spring to autumn foliage" — a FOLIAGE season, not a bloom season. Converted to Mar-Oct because that is what the research states and the card's band is the season of interest; the plant's yellow daisies are usually removed on a silver-foliage plant anyway (see prune).
